And so that this authority of ours may possess unbreakable and inviolate force, we have written it below with our own hand and ordered it authenticated by the impression of our ring.

Sign of Louis, most serene emperor.

I, Hirminmarus, notary, in the place of Hugo, have reviewed and subscribed.

Data given on the seventh day before the Ides of December, in the twenty-first year, Christ being favorable, of the reign of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the twelfth indiction. Done at Blanciaco, prosperously, in the name of the Lord. Amen.

## CLXXXIX. FOR THE SAME MONASTERY. (Year 854)

[In Schaten, in the same work, p. 97.]

In the name of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the divinely propitious clemency, emperor Augustus.

If, from the benefits bestowed upon us by God, we confer something through the gift of our generosity upon places dedicated to God, we firmly believe that this will profit us both for passing our mortal life happily and for attaining eternal life forever. Therefore we wish it to be known to the knowledge of all our faithful, present as well as future, that it has pleased our serenity to assign in their entirety to the monastery called Nova Corbeia, where at the present time the venerable abbot Warinus is recognized as pastor and rector, certain estates belonging to us, situated in Angaria, in Logni, whose names are Sulbichi and Hemlion, so that in the times of ourselves and our successors they may remain perpetually under the authority of that monastery, for providing the stipends of the monks established there and for supplying and relieving the needs of that monastery.

These estates, as we have said, with all their belongings, appurtenances, and boundaries, and with everything pertaining to them—that is, houses and other buildings, lands, meadows, woods, fields, pastures, waters and watercourses, cultivated and uncultivated places, movable property and self-moving animals, and dependents of diverse sex and age—we grant and confirm to the aforesaid monastery, so that from this day henceforth, as has been said, they may remain perpetually in its right and power, without contradiction or opposition from any count, public judge, or any other person. And so that this authority of our donation and grant may possess inviolable and unshaken firmness, we have confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our ring.

Sign of Louis, most serene emperor.

I, Hirminmarus, notary, acting in the place of Theogo, have examined and subscribed.

Given on the Ides of May, in the twenty-first year, Christ being favorable, of the reign of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the twelfth indiction. Done at the royal palace of Aachen, prosperously, in the name of God. Amen.

## CXC. FOR THE CHURCH OF GERONA. (Year 834)

[Flórez, *España sagrada*, vol. XLIII, p. 375, from the archive of the bishopric of Gerona.]

In the name of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the divinely propitious clemency, emperor Augustus.

If, for the love of God, we bestow suitable benefits upon places devoted to divine worship and upon those who serve God there, we do not doubt that a reward of eternal recompense will be repaid to us by the Lord. Therefore we wish it to be known to the understanding of all our faithful, present as well as future, that the venerable Wimer, bishop of the holy Church of Gerona, approaching our highness, requested that the aforesaid see, together with the estates and dependents granted to that see by our lord and father Charles and by other devout persons, which it is now known to possess—namely, in the county of Empúries, an estate called Olianus with its boundaries; and an estate called Cacavianus; and the old settlement of Celsianus, with the new village called Vellosos, with its castle and its territory; and in the county of Gerona, half of the estate of Mollero, and the estate of Milliasam, together with the other properties which it is known to have possessed there for a long time, as well as a third part of the pasture dues and tolls of that county; and other estates whose names are Castellum Fractum and Parietes Ruffini, with a third part of the pasture dues and tolls of that county; and an estate in the county of Besalú called Bascara, with its settlements and its territory, as well as Arcas, and a settlement called Spedulias, and another settlement lying within the boundaries of the aforesaid estates; and also other estates called Crispianus and Miliarias, with a third part of the pasture dues and tolls of that county—we should place under our protection and the defense of immunity because of the attacks of malicious men.

Granting his petition, and for the love of God, we place the aforesaid see, together with the estates listed above that presently remain in its possession, under our protection. We have also decreed that this authority of ours be made concerning that same see, by which we decree that no public judge, nor anyone exercising judicial authority, whether of higher or lower rank, may at any time dare to enter the churches, places, fields, or other possessions of the aforesaid see which it now lawfully possesses within the dominion of our empire, or which divine mercy may hereafter wish to increase in the right of that place, in order to hear or examine cases according to judicial custom, exact fines, impose lodgings or requisitions, take sureties, or constrain the men of that Church contrary to the order of justice; nor may anyone dare to exact any other payments or unlawful exactions, or in any way presume to withdraw what it legally holds in possession.

Rather, let the aforesaid bishop and his successors possess peacefully the properties of that Church, with everything it possesses, obey our command faithfully, and continually beseech the mercy of the Lord for us, our wife and sons, and the entire Christian people entrusted to us. And so that this authority of our confirmation may retain inviolable and unshaken firmness through the course of the years, we have confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our ring.

Sign of Louis, most serene emperor.

I, Maginarius, acting in the place of Hugo, have examined and subscribed.

[Col. 1248A]

Given on the fourth day before the Nones of December, in the twenty-first year, Christ being favorable, of the reign of our lord Louis, most serene emperor.

## CXCI. FOR THE MONASTERY OF KEMPTEN. (Year 834)

[Neugart, *Codex Alemannicus*, p. 217.]

[Note: Published from the original by R. P. Maximilian Rassler, S.J., in the appendix to *Vindiciae contra vindicias*, etc., p. 26. It also appears in the *Refutation of the Grievances of the City of Kempten*, entitled *Des Hochfürst. Stifts Kempten gründliche Widerlegung*, etc., 1737, proofs, p. 13. D. Bouquet reports a fragment, *Script. Rer. Gall.*, vol. VI, p. 595. Its opening is: “In the name of the Lord God and Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the divinely propitious clemency, emperor Augustus.”]

Diploma of Louis the Pious by which he placed “the monastery whose name is Capidona [Note: Kempten, the ducal abbey on the river Iller in the Allgäu.], where at the present time the venerable man Tatto is recognized as abbot, pastor, and rector, which is extremely poor in property [Note: That the resources of the people of Campidona had been reduced from the year 817 is clear from a decree of Louis the Pious issued at Aachen in that same year, where the monastery of Campita in Alemannia is still listed among those which were required to give only gifts, without military service. The decree was published by Sirmond, *Conc. Gall.*, vol. II, p. 685; Duchesne, *Script. Rer. Franc.*, vol. II, p. 323; Baluze, *Capit. reg. Franc.*, vol. I, p. 589; Mabillon, *Annal. Bened.*, book XXVIII, p. 436; Bouquet, *Script. Rer. Gall.*, vol. VI, p. 407.], and in which a considerable number of monks are maintained for serving God, under his protection and defense,” and declared it immune from all public functions and other burdens.

Sign of lord Louis, most pious emperor.

I, Hirminhardus [Note: Read *Hirminmaris* or *Hirminmarus*.], notary, acting in the place of Hugo, have examined and subscribed.

Given on the fifth day before the Nones of July, in the twenty-first year, Christ being favorable, of the reign of lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the twelfth indiction [Note: The indiction and the imperial year agree.]. Done at the royal palace of Aachen [Note: It may be gathered clearly enough from Thegan’s account of *The Deeds of Louis the Pious*, chapter 48 and following, that Louis the Pious was at Aachen at this time, having been rescued from the hands of Lothair by his like-named son and restored to the throne. He says that both celebrated the holy Easter of the Lord there and that, in the same year—which was the twenty-first year of his reign—the emperor granted pardon to all who had been compelled to abandon him.], prosperously, in the name of God. Amen.

## CXCII. FOR THE MONASTERY OF PRÜM. (Year 834)

[In Martène, *Amplissima Collectio*, p. 90, from the cartulary of Prüm.]

In the name of God and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the divinely propitious clemency, emperor Augustus.

[Note: Mabillon observes in *De re diplomatica*, book I, chapter 3, no. 13, that in his diplomas issued after his restoration to the throne Louis the Pious uses not *ordinante* or *propitiante*, as before, but *repropitiante*, since he had experienced God once again propitious toward him.]

If we bring the reasonable petitions of the servants of God to their desired effect, we not only make those servants of God more ready and devoted to beseech God’s mercy for us, but we also trust that by this act we shall merit the most merciful kindness of that same Lord. Therefore let the understanding of all our faithful, present as well as future, know that Marcuardus, venerable abbot of the monastery founded in honor of our Lord Jesus Christ the Savior by our grandfather, of blessed memory, the most glorious king Pippin, as a new foundation in the Ardennes above the river Prüm, came to our highness with certain monks from the congregation of that monastery. He explained to our clemency that our vassal Batericus, when he had decided to live monastically in the aforesaid monastery, had assigned to that monastery, by a solemn deed of donation confirmed by his own hand and by the hands of distinguished men, a certain estate belonging to him, which he had most recently received from our largesse as his own property and which is called Madalbodi-Sperarius.

So that it might be clear to us that this had indeed been done, they presented to our presence the authority of our grant by which that estate had been granted by us to the aforesaid Batericus as his own property, together with the deed of donation and transfer by which, when he sought the monastic life, he assigned this same estate to the aforesaid monastery and to the monks residing there. At the same time they requested and entreated us, for the sake of firmness, to order a precept of our authority to be made concerning those documents, because of the evasions of malicious persons.

Granting their petition, we ordered this precept of our authority to be made for the aforesaid venerable abbot Marcuardus, or for the benefit of his aforesaid monastery. By it we decree and command that no one of our faithful at any time presume to cause disturbance or bring any accusation concerning the aforesaid estate against the aforesaid Marcuardus or his successors. Rather, let the portion of the aforesaid monastery possess it in perpetual ownership, just as it was granted or transferred by us to the aforesaid Batericus as his own property, or just as it was assigned by that same Batericus to the same monastery by the deed of his transfer.

Let the aforesaid venerable abbot Marcuardus, his successors, and the monks residing in that monastery for generations be permitted to do concerning or within that estate whatever monastic discipline shall determine ought to be done. And so that this authority of our confirmation may possess perpetual firmness, we ordered it to be sealed below with our ring.

Sign of Louis, most serene Augustus.

Given on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of August, in the twenty-first year, Christ being favorable, of the reign of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the twelfth indiction. Done at the royal palace of Thionville, prosperously, in the name of God. Amen.

## CXCIII. FOR ALBERIC, BISHOP OF LANGRES. (Year 834)

[From *Gallia Christiana*, vol. IV, p. 130, proofs.]

In the name of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the divinely propitious clemency, emperor Augustus.

If we bring the just and reasonable petitions of priests and servants of God to their fulfillment, we not only exercise the royal and imperial custom, but also make those same persons more devoted and ready to beseech the mercy of the Lord for our transgressions. Therefore let it be known to all the faithful of the holy Church of God and to our own faithful, present and future, that Alberic, venerable bishop of the city of Langres, approaching our highness, represented to our gentleness concerning the bishopric of that city, formerly entrusted by us to him for governing the people of our Lord Jesus Christ, that he had found it greatly deprived, both inwardly and outwardly, in divine services as well as in human offices and ministries, in the institutions of the canons and the rules of holy life as well as in buildings and other necessities—partly through the negligence of its rectors, and partly through the slothfulness of its provosts—and almost entirely without the protection of any proper order.

He had nevertheless undertaken, as was fitting, with righteous, great, and strenuous labor, with all his strength, insofar as the Lord had granted him ability, and with immense zeal, to bring it to the standard of rectitude and dignity. He had also richly adorned the life of the canons serving the Lord there with canonical institutions, the stipends necessary for human frailty, and dwellings and cloisters of various kinds, so that their life might not thereafter decline in any respect. He had supported the estates and properties of that see by granting them, namely:

Two tenant holdings around the walls of that city; and in the same county of Langres, an estate called Marcilliacum with its church and appurtenances; and, in the same county, the estate called Hurbaniacum, as much as is known to belong to Saint Mammès in that estate, together with what is known to lie outside it but to pertain to the same estate, except for those properties known to be under the right and power of Saints Amator and Ferreolus; likewise, in the same county, at the place called Radalenis Bridge, twelve tenant holdings with everything pertaining to those holdings, together with a chapel; and, in the same county, the estate called Gregory’s Court, in its entirety; and at Ciddennacum, one tenant holding; and, in the same county, at several places, what noble persons had bestowed upon the table of the clergy by solemn donation; as well as the tenant holding situated in the estate of Primiacum, with vineyards; and, in the county of Bologna, in the estate called Helnone, six tenant holdings, both within and outside; and, in the counties of the Atoarii and of Dijon, specifically in the places called Sueconicus, Brigendonis, and Salcis, as much as the tenant Fluviolus of Saint Mammès appeared to possess in those places; and, in the county of Beaune, in the estate of Givriacum, a church with thirteen tenant holdings; and, in the same county, in the estate called Godoleni-Curtis, seven tenant holdings with everything pertaining to them; and, in the hundred of Hoscarineae, in the estate of Fisemis, a church and nine tenant holdings with everything pertaining to those holdings, and a vineyard called Plantas; and, in the same hundred, at the place called Spernacum, one tenant holding.

He earnestly beseeched the excellence of our imperial majesty that we should support his disposition and arrangement, which was in no way to be condemned, with the protection of our authority, and deign to strengthen it so that it might thereafter remain firm for everlasting times. Since we judged his petitions worthy, we were pleased to grant them, and we considered it appropriate to bring to fulfillment whatever he had requested, as stated above.

Accordingly, inspired by divine love, we ordered these letters of our authority to be made concerning the aforesaid see and the canons serving the Lord there for a long time. By them we decree and sanction that the places prescribed above, with everything justly and lawfully pertaining to them, just as they were bestowed upon the canons by the often-mentioned Alberic, venerable bishop of the aforesaid see, shall by this authority of ours remain in their right and power, serving their uses and various needs and enabling them to carry out divine worship more fully, without anyone diminishing or retracting them.

No successor of theirs, namely any rector of the aforesaid Church, may presume to take them away from their control or transfer them to any other place for any reason. Rather, let them use the aforesaid properties without anyone’s opposition for carrying out the service of our God and Lord; and let them arrange, dispose of, and justly [eff . . . . re] whatever pertains to their uses and needs in the service of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that, once every poverty of want has been removed, they may more eagerly delight in continually beseeching the mercy of the Lord for us, our wife and children, and the peace and stability of the whole empire entrusted to us by God. And so that this authority of our largesse and grant may be held firmly and better preserved for future times, we ordered it to be sealed below with our ring.

I, Hirminmarus, notary, acting in the place of Hugo, have examined and subscribed.

Given on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of September, in the twenty-first year, Christ being favorable, of the reign of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the twelfth indiction. Done at the city of Langres, prosperously, in the name of God. Amen.

## CXCIV. FOR THE MONASTERY OF SAINT SAVIOR AT REDON. (Year 834)

[In D. Bouquet, *Recueil des Histoires*, vol. VI, p. 597, from the proofs in *History of Brittany*, p. 29.]

In the name of [the Lord] God and Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the divinely propitious clemency, emperor Augustus.

If, for love of him by whose gift we have been preferred to other mortals, we raise up places consecrated to divine worship through suitable benefits of our magnificence, so that divine worship may be carried out more abundantly, we firmly believe that the Lord will reward us with the prize of divine recompense.

Therefore we wish it to be known to the understanding of all our faithful, present as well as future, that Conwoion, venerable abbot of the monastery called Redon, which he himself had built from its foundations, with our permission, in the county of Broërec, at the place called Bain [Note: Now a parish church near Redon.], and where he had established religious men to live according to the monastic life, approached our highness. With earnest prayers he requested that, for the love of our Lord Jesus Christ, in whose honor that monastery is known to be dedicated, we should bestow upon the same monastery, as our alms, some of the properties belonging to us, from which the brothers serving God in that monastery might obtain the necessary support.

Moved by his petition, and also urged by the prayer and intervention of our faithful Nominoe, it pleased our serenity, by this authority of ours, to grant to the aforesaid monastery and to the monks serving God there for enduring times the entire parish in which that same monastery is known to have been built, called Bain, as stated above, together with all its appurtenances; and also, in the same county, a small estate called Lant-Degon.

By this authority we decree that the aforesaid properties shall remain perpetually in their right and power, for their uses and various needs and for carrying out divine worship more fully, without anyone diminishing or retracting them. No one may presume to take them away from their control in any manner or transfer them to any other place for any reason.

Rather, let them use those same estates without anyone’s opposition for carrying out more diligently the service of our Lord God, and let them arrange, dispose of, and justly accomplish whatever pertains to their uses and needs in the service of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that, once every poverty of want has been removed, they may more eagerly delight in continually beseeching the mercy of the Lord for us, our wife and children, and the peace and stability of the whole empire entrusted to us by God.

And so that this authority of our largesse and consent may possess unchangeable and unshaken firmness, we have confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our ring.

Sign of Louis, most serene emperor.

I, Hirminmaris, notary, acting in the place of Hugo, have examined.

Given on the fifth day before the Kalends of December, in the twenty-first year, Christ being favorable, of the reign of lord Louis, most serene emperor, in the thirteenth indiction [Note: The indiction begins in the month of September.]. Done at the royal palace of Attigny, prosperously, in the name of God. Amen.

## CXCV. FOR THE DUSERENSIAN MONASTERY. (Year 835)

[In Chifflet, proofs to the *History of the Abbey of Tournus*, p. 262, and in D. Bouquet, vol. VI, p. 598.]

In the name of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the divinely propitious clemency, emperor Augustus.

When we strive to provide for places dedicated to God in whatever they may need, we trust that we thereby merit more abundantly the favor of him for whose love we are known to do this. Therefore we wish it to be known to all the faithful of the holy Church of God and to our own, present and future, that Hildigisus, abbot of the Duserensian monastery, approaching our gentleness, represented to our clemency that Warnarius, formerly a count, had given to that monastery a certain estate called Masteces, situated in the county of Tricastin, together with dependents and everything pertaining to it, or as much as he appeared to possess lawfully and by proprietary right in that county.

But since the aforesaid count, Warnarius by name, had acquired part of those properties jointly with a freewoman named Heldisnota, and, after her death, had acquired another part jointly with our bondwoman named Beltildis, he feared that the connection with that bondwoman might cause him some opposition concerning those properties. He therefore humbly sought our mercy, so that he might deserve to receive our authority concerning this matter, by which the rectors of that monastery might perpetually possess the aforesaid properties and dependents without anyone’s contradiction.

Since we judged his petition worthy, we were pleased, for the love of God, to grant it and to have this confirmation of our authority made. By it we decree and command that the aforesaid estate, together with its dependents and all its properties, appurtenances, and boundaries, and with everything justly and lawfully pertaining to it, or as much as the aforesaid count appeared to possess lawfully and by proprietary right in the aforesaid county, shall remain forever in the possession and control of that monastery and its rectors, just as the aforesaid count Warnarius formerly bestowed them upon our monastery, without anyone’s disturbance or opposition.

Nor should they fear that thereafter anything will be diminished or any harm inflicted upon those properties and dependents, or upon anything pertaining to them, by any judge or administrator of our treasury or of any other authority, whoever he may be. Thus may the monks serving God there delight in beseeching the mercy of the Lord more attentively for us, our wife and children, and the stability of the whole empire entrusted to us by God.

And so that the restoration by our majesty might henceforth be held firm, we decreed that this authority of ours be made concerning the aforesaid monastery of Saint Benedict, its rectors, and the monks dwelling there through the passing ages. By it we command and order that the aforesaid little estate, in its entirety, remain in the power and governance of the rectors of that monastery, and that it not be torn away or withdrawn from the control and power of that monastery by any of the faithful of the holy Church or by any of our own faithful.

Rather, let it serve, without anyone’s opposition, the uses of the monks serving God there, so that the brothers residing there in the service of our Lord Jesus Christ may more willingly and devoutly delight in beseeching his mercy for us, our wife and children, and the stability of the whole empire entrusted to us by God.

And so that this authority of our restoration and confirmation may, with the Lord’s protection, remain unshaken in our times and those to come, we ordered it to be sealed below with our ring.

I, Hirminmarius, notary, acting in the place of Hugo, have examined.

Given on the eighth day before the Kalends of September, in the twenty-second year, Christ being favorable, of the reign of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the thirteenth indiction.

Done at the royal palace of Cirsiacum [Note: Mabillon reads *Cusiacum*. Yet he had said above: “I find the cited diploma of Louis Augustus for the monastery of Fleury, given in the twenty-second year of his reign at the palace of Circiacum; and I have no doubt that this is Carisiacum.” The reading *Cirsiacum* or *Crisiacum* should be retained: it was a royal palace in the Ardennes, where, according to the Bertinian annalist, Louis hunted in autumn.], prosperously, in the name of God. Amen.

## CXCVI. FOR THE MONASTERY OF PRÜM. (Year 835)

[In Hantheim, *History of Trier*, vol. I, p. 178.]

In the name of the Lord and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the divinely propitious clemency, emperor Augustus.

If we confer some benefit through the gift of our generosity upon places dedicated to God, and relieve ecclesiastical needs at the petition of the servants of God with the help of our assistance, we firmly trust that this will profit us for happily attaining eternal blessedness. Therefore let the discernment and welfare of all the faithful of the holy Church of God and of our own, present as well as future, know that we have granted as their own property to the monastery called Prüm and to the monks serving God there, over whom the venerable abbot Marcuardus is recognized as presiding [Note: Marcuardus. We had still seen his predecessor Tancradus in 826. Yet he is reported to have died in 829 in the *Chronicle of Regino*, and Marcwardus, a prudent man devoted to sacred religion, succeeded him. It is not stated from which monastery he had been taken. Mabillon nevertheless observes in *Annals of the Benedictines*, book XXX, no. 34, that he was related to Lupus, abbot of Ferrières, born in Gaul, who in letter 91 calls Guago his son and nephew and Marcwardus his relative. Moreover, from Lupus’s letter 55 it is understood that Marcwardus had been enrolled in the community of Ferrières. In it Lupus asks Marcwardus to intercede with the emperor: “since you are from our place,” he says, “from which only ecclesiastical usefulness has withdrawn you bodily.”], properties belonging to us in the county of Worms, at the place called Albulfi Villa [Note: Albulfi Villa. This palace was situated near the village of Albesheim, by the little river Prüm, near Kirchheim, as the *Gottwicken Chronicle*, p. 881, shows. There, opposite the said village, remain Gaversheim and Stetten, which are named here as Gomurithesheim and Stetin. In the register of Caesar, abbot of Prüm, in Leibniz, *Collectio Etymologica*, part II, p. 336, it is written *Alvesheim* and so forth; the count of Leiningen holds its right of patronage from Prüm in fief.], namely, one demesne mansus; and at Gomurithesheim and also at Stetin, among these aforesaid places, thirteen mansi with dependents of both sexes residing there; and also the basilica built in the same Albulfi Villa, with the tithes legally pertaining to it from the estates written above.

We grant all this, completely and in its entirety, to the aforesaid monastery of Prüm and to the monks serving the Lord there, for relieving their various needs, moved by divine love and honor: namely, houses, buildings, vineyards, lands, woods, meadows, waters and watercourses, rights of exit and entry, and whatever property belonging to our right is known to exist in the aforesaid estate. Thus, whatever the rectors and ministers of that monastery may wish to do in or concerning these properties according to ecclesiastical law, let them have free power in all respects.

And so that this authority of our largesse and grant may possess inviolable and unshaken firmness, we have confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our ring.

Sign of Louis, most serene emperor.

I, Hirminmaris . . .

Given on the eighth day before the Kalends of June, in the twenty-second year, Christ being favorable, of the reign of lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the thirteenth indiction.

## CXCVII. FOR THE CHURCH OF LE MANS. (Year 835)

[In Baluze, *Miscellanea*, vol. I, p. 86.]

In the name of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the divinely propitious clemency, emperor Augustus.

If, for love of him by whose gift we have been preferred to other mortals, we raise up places consecrated to divine worship through suitable benefits of our munificence, so that divine worship may be carried out more abundantly, we firmly believe that the Lord will reward us with the prize of a worthy recompense.

Therefore we wish it to be known to the goodwill of all our faithful, present as well as future—namely, bishops, abbots, dukes, counts, household officials, and administrators of both higher and lower rank, whether ecclesiastical or public—that it has pleased our highness to grant, as a gift of our largesse, a certain cell situated in the county of Le Mans, in the suburb of that city, that is, between the river Sarthe and the wall of the aforesaid city.

It is constructed and dedicated in honor of holy Mary, Mother of God, and of the holy apostle Peter, and of the other saints whose relics and memories are venerated there. We grant it in its entirety, with all its properties, appurtenances, and boundaries, and with everything pertaining to it—that is, basilicas, houses and other buildings, vineyards, lands, meadows, woods, fields, pastures, waters and watercourses, mills, cultivated and uncultivated places, movable and immovable property, self-moving animals, and dependents of diverse sex and age—to the mother and city church of Le Mans, founded and dedicated in honor of the holy Savior, the aforesaid holy Mary ever-virgin, and the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, as well as Saint Stephen, where at the present time the venerable man and our faithful Aldricus is recognized as pastor and rector.

We transfer it from our right into the right and power of that church by solemn donation, so that the servants and dependents of God residing there may be more abundantly provided with the stipends necessary for them, and so that the needs of that church, both external and internal, may more easily be supplied.

By this authority of ours, through which we assign the aforesaid cell, with everything pertaining to it as stated above, to the aforesaid mother and city church and to Aldricus, bishop of that see, we command and prohibit that no one, either in our times or in those of our successors, presume to withdraw, usurp, or invade that same cell. Rather, let it remain perpetually in the possession and authority of the aforesaid Church, of the aforementioned Aldricus, bishop of that church, and of his episcopal successors, for carrying out and completing the matters stated above.

And so that this authority of our grant and transfer may possess perpetual firmness of its force, we have confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with the impression of our ring.

Sign of Louis, most serene emperor.

I, Hirminmarus, notary, acting in the place of Hugo, have examined and subscribed.

Given on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the twenty-third year, Christ being favorable, of the reign of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the fourteenth indiction. Done at the royal palace of Aachen, prosperously, in the name of God. Amen.

## CXCVIII. FOR THE SAME CHURCH. (Year 835)

[In Baluze, same work, p. 87.]

In the name of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the divinely propitious clemency, emperor Augustus.

If we lend an ear to the just and reasonable petitions of priests and servants of God, and bring them to their desired fulfillment, we not only exercise royal and imperial custom, but also make those same men more devoted and ready to entreat the Lord’s mercy for our transgressions; and through this we confidently believe that God’s immense mercy can more readily be reconciled to us. Therefore we wish it to be known to all the faithful of God’s holy Church and to our own, present and future, that Aldricus, venerable bishop of the city of Le Mans, represented to our Excellence that the monastery of Saint Mary and Saint Peter, situated outside the walls of the aforesaid city and founded and built by his predecessor, Bishop Innocent, from the property and resources of his bishopric, had subsequently, through the intervention of certain circumstances, been withdrawn from the right of the said see and had until now been withheld from its control.

And so that what he asserted might become truthfully apparent to us, he brought before the eyes of our majesty certain documentary records [Col. 1256D] and certain charters of kings—namely, of our predecessors. When these had been examined, it was clearly shown that the aforesaid monastery belonged to the right of the aforementioned see of Le Mans entrusted to him, and ought to remain under its control. He humbly implored our gentleness that what was declared by such evident indications might also be strengthened by our assent, or rather by our authority anew.

Having thus learned the matter more clearly, and judging it fitting to extend the favor of our majesty to him for the love of God and in reverence for the same holy see, we ordered this precept of our authority to be made and given to him and to his successors in that office for all time. By it we decree and sanction that the aforesaid monastery of Saint Mary and Saint Peter, which for some time had been withdrawn from their right and jurisdiction, shall henceforth be held and possessed by them, and that they shall have free power to dispose of it in whatever way they wish according to ecclesiastical custom. Nor shall it thereafter be separated by any occasion or violence from the right of the aforesaid see or of its rectors; rather, with everything belonging or pertaining to it, it shall perpetually remain wholly and sincerely under the authority, disposition, and will of that see and its rectors, so that divine worship may be more diligently carried out.

And so that this authority of our restoration may possess perpetual firmness, we confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it sealed with the impression of our ring.

**Louis.**

I, Hirminmarus, notary, in the place of Hugo, have examined and subscribed.

Given on the eleventh day before the Kalends of April, in the twenty-third year, with Christ favorable, of the reign of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the fourteenth indiction. Done at the royal palace of Aachen, successfully, in God’s name. Amen.

## CXCIX. FOR THE SAME CHURCH. (Year 834.)

[In Baluze, same work, p. 87.]

In the name of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the clemency of God granting renewed favor, emperor Augustus.

If we willingly lend our ears to the petitions of priests concerning any ecclesiastical necessities, and with God’s help bring them to fulfillment, we clearly believe that this will benefit us in attaining the rewards of eternal recompense. Therefore we wish it to be known to the understanding of our faithful, both present and future, and also to our successors, that Aldricus, bishop of the city of Le Mans, approaching our serenity, made known to us how long ago, because sins had obstructed its affairs, the holy mother church which stands in that city, dedicated to God in honor of the holy Mother of God Mary and of the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, where formerly there had been many possessions, had been so humbled and stripped of its property that the treasury of that church had been taken from it by most Christian princes, while certain documentary charters by which property and dependents had been assigned to the same church had, through the events of various misfortunes, largely perished there. Moreover, because poverty had intervened as an obstacle, the office of divine worship had been lamentably abandoned, and the church itself had remained for so long in that pitiable collapse—or rather destitution—until, by the Lord’s inspiration, our lord and father of holy memory, Charles, most noble and orthodox emperor, returned to that church certain small monasteries and villas belonging to the same bishopric, together with other possessions, through the intercession of many nobles and of his own leading men. Strengthened by these, that holy place now serves divine power freely and without excuse.

The aforesaid bishop therefore asked us to decree that, for the sake of firmness, a precept of our authority and immunity concerning that holy place should be made for those same small monasteries and possessions—which our aforesaid father and we later restored to the church—as well as for those which the aforementioned church had previously held lawfully and legally, so that the church might hold, possess, and defend the aforesaid property more firmly and securely in present and future times. He also showed us a precept of our father, of good memory, the blessed lord Charles, in which the same things were individually named as in ours, except only those which we later restored from the right of the aforesaid church, for the love of God and in reverence for the saints, to the venerable Bishop Aldricus and to the aforesaid mother church through precepts of our authority.

We willingly assented to his petition for the love of God and in reverence for that holy place, and judged that this precept of our authority concerning it should be made. By it we order that the same small monasteries, possessions, and dependents, with everything belonging or pertaining to them, which the church now holds justly and legally—whether those which our father and we restored to that church, or those which formerly belonged to the right of the same bishopric—the church shall hold and defend firmly and inviolably by this authority of ours; namely, the cell of Saint Vincent with everything belonging to it, and the cell of Saint Albinus, as well as the cell of Saint Audoenus, the cell of Saint Rigomerus, the cell of Saint Almerus, the cell of Saint Ulfacius, and the cell of Saint Baumadus.

All these, with everything belonging to them, together with the canonical villages, namely Salica, Montiniacum, Cocciacum, Placiacum, and Oxellum, as well as Anciacum and Artinis, together with the other villages whose names are inserted in the full records of the aforesaid mother church; with the chief estates and the other small estates belonging to them, as they are contained in the full records of the aforementioned mother church, namely Rupiacum, Canania, Culturas, Baliavaliancion, Colonica, Vetusiacum, and the canonical village of Celsiacum; and the villa of the same bishopric, as well as Aloniacum, Asinarias, and Vodebeis, namely Callemartium, or the other small estates whose names are not immediately available but are inserted in the full records of the aforesaid holy mother church; and the census of all the villages situated in the same parish, as is recorded in the full records and summaries of that church; moreover, the monastery of Saint Carilefus situated in the district of Labricus, with everything belonging to it; and the small monastery situated between the walls of the aforesaid city and the River Sarthe, built and dedicated in honor of the holy Savior, the holy Mother of God Mary, the holy apostles, and the other saints.

These two small monasteries, for the love of God and affection for the aforementioned Bishop Aldricus, we have restored to the aforesaid mother church, with everything belonging to them, to be perpetually possessed and held. We have also restored to the aforesaid church the canonical village of Conedralium in its entirety, and the villa called Brogilus or Novavilla, with its forests, small estates, and everything belonging to it.

We have also restored to it Lugdunum, Calisa, Tridentum, Bonalla, and Baladon, together with the benefices of five of our vassals, namely Vestadigbei, Mundi, Wolfardus, Bodo, and his associate, with everything belonging or pertaining to them, as is contained in the precepts of ours which we ordered to be made and written concerning the aforesaid small monasteries and estates, or concerning those pertaining to the aforementioned Bishop Aldricus.

All these things, for the love of God and in reverence for the saints, we have restored and confirmed as a matter of justice, as our alms, to the venerable Bishop Aldricus and to the aforesaid mother church, which the aforementioned Aldricus enlarged and rebuilt, as it were, from its foundations, nobly adorned, and solemnly consecrated and reconciled in honor of the Lord Savior, of his holy Mother Mary, and of the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, as well as Saint Stephen. We have judged that they are to be held under the right of the same church and under the control of its rectors, and ecclesiastically governed.

Therefore, by this authority of ours, we again confirm to that church the aforementioned small monasteries, cells, and estates, with all the property and dependents belonging to them, which the aforesaid church now holds justly and legally, under the protection of our immunity.

Therefore, ordering, we command that no public judge, no one exercising judicial authority, nor any of our faithful, shall ever dare to enter the aforesaid villages, places, lands, or other possessions of the aforementioned Church—which it is known presently to hold and possess justly in any counties and territories under the authority of our kingdom, and which divine piety may hereafter wish to increase in the right of that holy place—for the purpose of hearing or bringing lawsuits, demanding or collecting tributes or fines, imposing lodging or provisions, exacting tolls, taking sureties, unjustly distraining the men of that church, whether free or enslaved, who appear to reside upon its land, or seeking any prohibitions or unlawful pretexts; nor shall anyone presume to exact any of the foregoing from the aforesaid property in any place.

Whatever the fisc could hope to receive from the property of the aforesaid Church, we grant in its entirety to that Church. Moreover, at the request of the aforesaid bishop, we ordered the following to be inserted in this precept, just as we find it inserted in the precept of our lord and father Charles, emperor of good memory: no judge, count, or any man or person whatsoever shall presume to accuse the ministers or advocates of the aforesaid church in a public court before first summoning the ministers of its possessions, the judges of the villages, and the men by whom he has been injured, so that he may receive familiar and just justice from them. If he is unable to receive his justice from the aforesaid ministers, then he shall summon the bishop of the aforementioned Church, so that he may receive from him familiar, good, and just justice.

And if he is unable to receive his justice either from that bishop or from his ministers, then afterward he shall have permission to seek his complaints justly, reasonably, and lawfully in a public court. But if, before doing this, he presumes to accuse or prosecute the bishop of the church of the aforesaid see, or his ministers and advocates, in a court or in a public assembly of any kind, because he has despised or violated our command, our precept, and our prohibition, he shall pay our royal fine to us on this account, and shall pay one hundred silver solidi to the bishop of the aforesaid church or to his ministers, and afterward shall receive his justice without legal penalty or any composition.

For the sake of God’s love and in reverence for the saints, we have granted the aforesaid legal jurisdictions to the bishops of the aforementioned church and to the servants of God serving the Lord there, and we wish them to remain granted for future times.

Again and again ordering, we command that none of our faithful, no public judge, nor any person appointed or substituted for office, shall in our times or in those of our successors presume to cause any disturbance or unjust opposition to the aforesaid church concerning the small monasteries, cells, possessions, dependents, and censuses, or concerning those things which divine piety may hereafter wish to increase for that church, whether from us, from our successors, or from other God-fearing persons. Rather, under this precept of our confirmation and protection, these things shall always be held quietly, peacefully, and justly as our alms under the right of the same bishopric, and shall be capable of being legally protected, so that whatever the rectors or ministers of that church wish to do with the aforesaid property for its need and benefit, they may enjoy entirely free discretion to do it. Thus may the bishops of that see, with the flock entrusted to them, continually entreat the Lord’s mercy with their most grateful prayers for our safety, that of our wife and offspring, and for the stability of the empire granted to us by God, which by his immense compassion he is to preserve.

And so that this authority may possess inviolable and unshakable firmness through the course of the years, we confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it sealed with the impression of our ring.

**Sign of Louis, most pious emperor.**

I, Maginarius, notary, in the place of Hugo, have examined and subscribed.

[Col. 1260D]

Given on the Kalends of March, in the twenty-third year, with Christ favorable, of the reign of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the third indiction. Done in the public city of Poitiers, successfully, in God’s name. Amen.

## CC. FOR THE MONASTERY OF AUXERRE. (Year 835.)

[In Mabillon, *Acta Ordinis S. Benedicti*, century IV, part II, p. 576.]

In the name of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the clemency of God granting renewed favor, emperor Augustus.

If we favor the just and reasonable petitions of the servants of God which they bring to the ears of our majesty, for the love of divine worship, we have complete confidence that we thereby more readily reconcile his mercy to us. Therefore we wish it to be known to all the faithful of God’s holy Church and to our own, present and future, that Christianus, venerable abbot of the monastery of Saint Germanus, confessor of Christ, situated in the suburb of Auxerre, approaching the serenity of our majesty, represented to our gentleness that his predecessor, the abbot named Deusdedit, had long ago petitioned our clemency to grant by a precept of our authority permission for himself and the monks living in the same monastery under his rule to choose an abbot from among themselves, according to the Rule of Saint Benedict, whenever abbots departed this life in accordance with human frailty.

We, assenting to his reasonable prayers, not only granted that permission for divine love, but also confirmed it anew by our imperial precept. But because, he confessed, the same writing of our confirmation had slipped from his possession and been lost through certain storms arising from an opposing party, he begged our clemency in the humblest prayers that he might deserve to receive the aforesaid authority rewritten through the abundance of our favor and kindness.

Judging his supplications worthy and reasonable, we were pleased to lend him an ear. Therefore we decreed that these letters of our authority should be made and given concerning the aforesaid Christian abbot and the monks living under the regular habit in the aforementioned monastery of Saint Germanus, confessor of the Lord, through the passing of time. By them we order and command that whenever any abbot of the same monastery departs this human life by divine calling, they shall have permission to choose an abbot from among themselves, if one can be found among them who is able to preside over them and benefit them according to the regular order.

Thus, preserving the norm of the regular order wholly through his most holy administration—or rather striving to fulfill it—may it please them to entreat the Lord’s mercy more attentively and peacefully, with unwearied prayers, for us, our wife and offspring, and the stability and peace of the entire empire entrusted to us by God.

And so that this authority of our command may possess inviolable and unshakable firmness in our times and those of our successors, we confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it marked with the impression of our ring.

[Col. 1261D]

Given on the fourth day before the Kalends of August, in the twenty-second year, with Christ favorable, of the reign of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the thirteenth indiction. Done at the villa of Luco, successfully, in God’s name. Amen.

## CCI. FOR THE CHURCH OF SAINT MARCELLUS OF CABILONUM. (Year 835.)

[From the cartulary of this church, in D. Bouquet, vol. VI, p. 601.]

In the name of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the clemency of God granting renewed favor, emperor Augustus.

[Col. 1262A]

If we lend an ear to the just and reasonable petitions of our faithful, which they wish to bring to our ears for the needs of the churches entrusted to them, and bring them to their desired fulfillment, we not only exercise royal and imperial custom, but also make those same faithful of ours more zealous in preserving their loyalty toward our interests, and make the priests and servants of God in those churches, who entreat the Lord’s mercy for our transgressions, more ready and devoted.

Therefore we wish it to be known to the understanding of all the faithful of God’s holy Church and of our own, both present and future, that Count Warinus, under whose care and governance we have the monastery of Saint Marcellus, which is known to have been built in a village called [Col. 1262B] Hubiliacus, approaching our majesty, informed our gentleness that he and his predecessors had granted certain possessions of that monastery to the canons serving God in the same monastery, to support and relieve their various necessities; namely, the villa called Floriacus, situated in the county of Magnimontum, in its entirety and with everything belonging to it; and in the county of Cabilonum, in the place called Boserontium, twelve manses with everything belonging to them.

He earnestly implored the excellence of our imperial majesty to strengthen their acts by our confirmation, so that henceforth they might remain inviolable for all time. We were pleased to assent to his supplication, which we judged worthy, and did not consider it inappropriate to bring about what he had requested, as was stated above.

Therefore, inspired by divine love, we ordered these letters of our authority to be made concerning the aforesaid canons, who serve the Lord in the aforementioned monastery for long ages. By them we decree and sanction that the aforesaid property—namely, the aforementioned villa and the aforesaid manses—with everything justly and legally belonging to them, just as they were granted to the aforesaid canons by Count Warinus and his aforementioned predecessors, shall by this authority of ours remain in their right and power, serving their own uses and various necessities for the more zealous performance of divine worship, without diminution or withdrawal of any kind.

[Note: [Col. 1261D] It should read: “the aforesaid property … and the aforementioned manses.”]

No successor of theirs, namely, any rector of the aforesaid monastery, shall presume in any way to take them away from their control or transfer them to any place on any pretext. Rather, let it be permitted to them to use the aforesaid possessions without anyone’s opposition for the more diligent service of the Lord and our God, and to arrange, dispose of, and justly carry out whatever pertains to their uses and necessities in the service of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Thus, once every scarcity of need has been removed, may it please them to entreat the Lord’s mercy continually and more attentively for us and our wife, and for the peace and stability of the entire empire entrusted to us by God.

And so that this authority of our confirmation may possess perpetual force, we ordered it sealed below with our ring.

**Sign of Louis, most serene Augustus.**

I, Hirminmarus, notary, in the place of Hugo, have examined.

Given on the sixth day before the Kalends of August, in the twenty-second year, with Christ favorable, of the reign of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, successfully, in God’s name. Amen.

## CCII. FOR THE MONASTERY OF SITHIU. (Year 835.)

[In Mabillon, *De re diplomatica*, p. 633.]

In the name of the Lord God and Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the clemency of God granting renewed favor, emperor Augustus.

If we permit the prayers of our faithful, who devoutly serve us, to reach their desired fulfillment through the accustomed generosity of our benevolence, we believe that we ought all the more to bring to completion, with a most worthy expression of our own honor, the petitions of our beloved brother Hugo, venerable abbot, which we do not doubt are wholly reasonable—especially those which are recognized to pertain to the more zealous performance of divine worship through the manifest fervor of his devotion.

Therefore let the understanding of all the faithful of God’s holy Church and of our own, both present and future, know that our aforementioned beloved brother Hugo, arch-notary of our sacred palace and venerable abbot of the monastery of Sithiu, situated in the county of Tervanum, [Col. 1263C] built in honor of the blessed ever-virgin Mary, Mother of our Lord Jesus Christ, and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, where the bodies of Christ’s confessors Audomarus and Bertinus are also known to be buried, made known to our Highness how long ago, in the time of his predecessor, Fridugis the abbot, we had issued our authority to that monastery. By it, following the paternal and ancestral custom, we placed it, with everything belonging to it, under our protection and mundeburd, and under the protection of our immunity; and we decreed by imperial authority that all its cells, villas, and other possessions situated in any counties and territories under the authority of our empire should not be divided by any of our successors or converted to other uses, and that the household of the same monastery should give no fodder to any persons whatsoever. He asked that we order this same authority of ours to be renewed in his name also.

Therefore, for the love of God and in reverence and honor for those same saints, and also at the admonition of our brother, we judged that our aforesaid authority concerning the same place and its successive rectors should be renewed through the passage of time, and that what had been decreed there should also be strengthened by the present authority.

Accordingly, we ordered these imperial letters of ours to be made, by which we admonish our successors that, just as we have granted the aforesaid monastery of Saint Mary and of Saints Peter and Paul, and of the blessed confessors of Christ Audomarus and Bertinus, to remain secure and stable, so they shall permit it to remain secure and stable. They shall not divide, or permit anyone to divide, its monasteries, cells, villas, or other possessions situated in any counties or territories, nor shall they turn those possessions to other uses.

We also sanction and decree by these imperial letters that no public judge, nor anyone exercising judicial authority, shall ever dare to enter the churches, places, lands, or other possessions of the aforementioned monastery which it presently possesses justly and legally in any counties or territories under the authority of our empire—or which divine piety may hereafter wish to increase in the right of that holy place—for the purpose of hearing lawsuits according to judicial custom, exacting fines, imposing lodging or provisions, demanding fodder, taking sureties, distraining the men of that monastery, whether free or enslaved, or seeking any restitutions or unlawful pretexts; nor shall anyone presume to exact any of the things mentioned above.

Rather, let the aforesaid abbot and his successors, or the men of the aforementioned monastery, as is contained in the precept of our lord and father, possess peacefully, under the protection of our immunity, all the fines and royal bans granted to them. Thus may those servants of God who serve the Lord there delight continually to entreat the Lord’s mercy for us and our offspring, and also for the stability of our entire empire, granted to us by God and to be preserved by him.

And so that this authority may, with the Lord’s protection, remain unshakable in our times and in future times, we confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it marked with the impression of our ring.

**Sign of Louis, most serene emperor.**

I, Hirminmarus, notary, in the place of Hugo the abbot, have examined and subscribed.

Given on the Ides of August, in the twenty-first year of the reign of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the tenth indiction. Done at the royal palace of Aachen, successfully, in God’s name. Amen.

## CCIII. FOR THE MONASTERY OF FLEURY. (Year 835.)

[In D. Bouquet, p. 604.]

[Col. 1264D]

In the name of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the clemency of God granting renewed favor [Note: [Col. 1263D] “By grace granting renewed favor,” in Mabillon, who published that precept in book VI of *De re diplomatica*, p. 522], emperor Augustus.

When the servants of God, compelled by some necessity, strive to bring their petitions before the ears of our clemency, we take care to extend to them the favor of imperial excellence for the love of him whose service they are known continually to perform. Without doubt, we believe that we thereby reconcile the mercy of him in whose honor and love we effectively undertake this work [Note: [Col. 1264D] For id efficaciter (“this effectively”), the same edition has id efficere (“to do this”)].

Therefore we wish it to be known to all the faithful of God’s holy Church and to our own, present and future, [Col. 1265A] how Boso, venerable abbot of the monastery of Saint Benedict, which is built in the county of Orléans, together with the congregation entrusted to him, made known to our Highness that our grandfather, King Pippin of good memory, thinking of the salvation of his soul and of that of his brother Carloman, and of the abolition of their sins and the attainment of the rewards of blessed and eternal life, had assigned to the aforesaid monastery of Saint Benedict, by a precept of his authority, a certain villa belonging to him called Suncampus [Note: [Col. 1265D] In Mabillon, Suncantus, commonly Souchamp], with its dependencies, villas, and boundaries belonging to it.

After he had then been taken from human affairs by divine calling, one of his vassals, named Gislearius, who had possessed the aforesaid villa by beneficiary right, after lawful transfer and vesting of that villa, with everything belonging or pertaining to it, had been made to the aforesaid monastery of Saint Benedict, usurped for possession by beneficiary right and unjustly occupied certain small estates belonging or pertaining to the aforesaid villa, whose names are Mairulfi-villa, Sigini-villa, Haderbaldi-villa, Enveri-villa, Catonis-villa, and Frondonis-villa [Note: [Col. 1265D] In the same author: Marrulfi-villa, Sigivi-villa, Hadrebledi-villa, Numeri-villa, Cathenis-villa, and Frondonis-villa; commonly Mairouville, Sainville, Arbouville, Evrinville, Chatonville, and Frouville]. Thus, as time progressed, they had slipped from the right of the aforesaid monastery.

But when we had sent our envoys to investigate this matter and report it to us—namely, Jonas, venerable bishop of Orléans, and Hugo, illustrious count—and when it became clearer than daylight, both from their report and from reading the precept of our aforementioned grandfather, that the aforesaid villas had been unjustly taken away from the right of the aforementioned monastery, it pleased us, for the remedy of our soul, to restore them with everything belonging to them to the same monastery.

And so that this authority of our donation may be held more firmly and be better preserved for future times, we ordered it sealed below with our ring.

I, Hirminmarus, notary, in the place of Hugo, have examined and subscribed.

Given on the second day before the Nones of January [Note: [Col. 1266D] Here the beginning of the reign is to be reckoned from the month of September of the year 813], in the twenty-second year, with Christ favorable, of the reign of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the thirteenth indiction. Done at the villa of Theodon, the royal palace, successfully, in God’s name. Amen.

## CCIV. FOR THE MONASTERY OF PRÜM. (Year 835.)

[Col. 1265D] Concerning the exchange made by Eberharius and Abbot Marcuardus.

[In Martène, *Amplissima Collectio*, vol. I, col. 94.]

In the name of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the clemency of God granting renewed favor, emperor Augustus.

If we confirm by our edicts things which faithful subjects of our empire have exchanged among themselves for their own needs, we exercise imperial custom and wish this to remain thereafter established by the firmest right. Therefore let the understanding of all our faithful, [Col. 1266A] present and future, know that Marcuardus, venerable abbot of the monastery called Prüm, made known to our Highness that he had exchanged certain property and dependents with two men named Heberarius and Hebrardus, for the advantage of both parties.

Accordingly, with our permission, the aforesaid venerable Abbot Marcuardus gave from the property of the aforementioned monastery, in the counties of Anjou and Retz, in the places called Hulmontillus, Carmarias, Boscus, and Tillus, to the aforesaid Heberarius and Hebrardus, to be held perpetually as their own, whatever property of the same monastery might be held there by right.

Conversely, in compensation for those same possessions, the aforesaid Heberarius and his brother Hebrardus gave from their own property to the aforementioned venerable Abbot Marcuardus, for the portion of his aforesaid monastery, in the county of Noyon, in the villa called Roccesheim, whatever they possessed in that villa or in the boundary of that villa by proprietary right—namely, a lordly courtyard with the buildings situated upon it, containing eighty-two jornales of demesne arable land and six proprisi, [Note: [Col. 1266D] *Proprisus*, or *porprisum* and *purprisum*, is a Germanic word which Goldastus interprets as “seized” or “violently occupied”] in which there are one hundred and twenty jornales, together with the dependents residing there, whose number and names are fully contained in the exchanges made by them.

They also gave in the villa called Husfileidesheim one courtyard, to which belong eighteen jornales of arable land, three cartloads of hay-producing meadow, eight jornales of forest in the *porprisa*, and another common forest which is not *proprisa*.

Likewise, in the county of Worms, in the villa called Haskmundesheim, one courtyard and twenty-eight jornales of vineyards, from which three cartloads of wine are gathered; and in Dionenheim and Rodulfisheim, vineyards sufficient to gather two cartloads of wine. And in Batenheim, one courtyard and a vineyard sufficient to gather one cartload of wine.

All the things named above, together with dependents, meadows, forests, pastures, waters, and watercourses, as is contained in the exchanges made by them, wholly and in their entirety, acquired and to be acquired, as stated above, the aforesaid men Heberarius and Hebrardus transferred to the aforementioned venerable Abbot Marcuardus for the portion of the aforesaid monastery, so that they might remain perpetually under its right. [The supplied Latin prints praescriptis hominibus Heberario et Hebrardo in the dative case (“to the aforesaid men Heberarius and Hebrardus”); the preceding description of their reciprocal grant indicates that these men are the donors here.]

Accordingly, two exchanges, written in identical form and strengthened by the hands of the parties and of other good men, were brought before our eyes for rereading. But for complete firmness they petitioned our Highness that we should confirm those same exchanges more fully anew by a precept of our gentleness.

We did not wish to deny assent to their petitions. Rather, know that just as we have granted and confirmed everything to each of our faithful who petitions justly and reasonably, so we have granted it to them and confirmed it in every respect.

Therefore, ordering, we command that whatever one party has transferred justly and reasonably to the other party, it shall henceforth hold and possess by the firmest right under this authority of ours, and that regarding whatever it decides to do with it, it shall enjoy entirely free discretion to act.

And so that this authority of our confirmation may remain inviolable, we ordered it sealed below with our ring.

I, Hirminmarus, notary, in the place of Hugo, have examined.

Given on the fourth day before the Ides of September, in the twenty-second year, with Christ favorable, of the reign of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the thirteenth indiction. Done at the monastery of Prüm, successfully, in God’s name. Amen.

## CCV. FOR ALDRICUS, ARCHBISHOP OF SENS, CONCERNING THE ABBEY [Col. 1267B] OF SAINT REMIGIUS. (Year 835.)

[From manuscript notes of the library of Saint-Germain-des-Prés, in D. Bouquet, vol. VI, p. 605.]

In the name of God and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the clemency of God granting renewed favor, emperor Augustus.

For if we diligently and most devotedly provide, with imperial foresight, for whatever pertains to the peace and quiet of the servants of God, we do not doubt that this contributes to the benefit of our soul and to the attainment of eternal blessedness. Therefore we wish it to be known to all the faithful of the holy Church of God and to our own, present as well as future, that Aldricus, venerable archbishop of the city of Sens, brought to the attention of our gentleness a certain monastery of his aforesaid bishopric, which had been established beside the walls of that same city in honor of blessed Remigius, confessor of Christ. Since, on account of certain hindrances which the monks serving the Lord there seemed to suffer because of the proximity and constant presence of the aforesaid city, he had caused it to be transferred to another place called Valliculas [or, Vallilias], namely, eight miles from that same city, he testified that Hrotta, formerly the wife of Count Meginarius, had assigned that place to the monastery of the aforesaid Saint Remigius by way of a donation, for the repose and remedy of herself and her husband.

But so that the monks whom he had caused to migrate from the aforesaid place would not at any time be compelled to suffer any opposition or disturbance from bishops succeeding one another in that see as the years passed, he professed that, while established in the city of the Wangiones together with his venerable fellow bishops, our faithful, from various churches, he had made for them a privilege by ecclesiastical authority. This became entirely clear when it was examined and reread. In it, with the firm agreement of all, he had decreed that none of the bishops succeeding him should presume to diminish anything from the possessions which they had held while dwelling in the former place, or impose upon them greater services than they had endured under him. Rather, they were to be permitted to possess in peace the properties assigned to the aforesaid monastery through the most religious devotion of the faithful, and no greater burden was to be imposed upon them than that which was known to have been established in the aforesaid privilege, confirmed together with those venerable bishops.

Although he foresaw that his ecclesiastical and pontifical constitution was firm through its own—and indeed divine—authority, he nevertheless judged it neither improper nor unreasonable that our imperial authority should also decree that his constitution remain perpetually firm. Accordingly, we have ordered these imperial letters of our authority to be drawn up concerning the aforesaid monastery. Through them we decree and command that, just as it was established by the aforesaid venerable Archbishop Aldricus, with the agreement of his reverend fellow bishops, worthy of the highest honor, and confirmed by a privilege strengthened by the hands of those same and many other priests of Christ and abbots, so henceforth, through this our authority, it shall remain fixed and unshaken [Col. 1268B] and inviolable.

Nor shall any of the bishops who, with Christ’s favor, succeed one another in the aforesaid city as time passes presume to diminish or alter anything of these provisions, or to increase the services beyond what has been inserted in the aforesaid privilege. Rather, the monks who from time to time serve the Lord there shall be permitted to live peacefully and regularly under the conditions prescribed in the privilege just mentioned, and continually to implore the Lord’s mercy more earnestly on behalf of us, our wife and offspring, and the stability of the empire entrusted to us and preserved by God. And so that this authority of our confirmation may retain unshaken and inviolable force both in our times and in those of our successors, we ordered it to be authenticated below with the impression of our ring.

[Col. 1268C]

Sign of Louis, most serene Augustus.

I, Hirminmarus, notary, have reviewed this in place of Hugo.

Given on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of December, in the twenty-second year of the reign, with Christ’s favor, of our lord Louis, most pious Augustus, in the thirteenth indiction. Done at the royal palace of Aachen, prosperously in the name of God. Amen.

## CCVI. LOTHAR’S CHARTER FOR THE MONASTERY OF SAINT AMBROSE OF MILAN (Year 835)

[Ughelli, *Italia sacra*, vol. IV, p. 80.]

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, the eternal God, Lothar, by the providence ordained by God, emperor Augustus.

[Col. 1268D]

The more excellently humanity flourishes when placed in a position of preeminence, the more diligently it ought to fulfill divine service, and the more earnestly to hear and carry out, with devoted willingness, every request of the faithful that pertains to this end, so that, by dealing well with the wishes of the Giver in accordance with what has been entrusted, it may, with His merciful help, pass happily through the present life and merit happily to attain the eternal blessings bestowed by His ineffable compassion.

Accordingly, when our beloved wife Hirmingardis, solicitous for divine matters and most diligently and assiduously urging our clemency to increase our munificence toward places dedicated to God, undertook to press this request more insistently out of affection for her brother, a boy of distinguished character named Hugo, she strove to persuade us that, for the increase of our piety and the enlargement of our reward, we should bestow certain benefits upon the place where he had been buried, namely the cemetery of Saint Ambrose, for the adornment of its lights and the provision of ornaments for the church, for the increase of our reward and the accumulation of blessedness for the aforesaid boy.

Therefore, let the discernment of all the faithful of the holy Church of God and of our own, present and future, know that, wishing to honor the prayers and wishes of that beloved wife of ours, we granted our assent. Accordingly, for the remedy of that boy, we bestow our beneficence upon the same holy place: a certain estate named Lemonta, with its indominical demesne and a chapel belonging to it, dedicated in honor of Saint Genesius, as well as olive groves and holdings, together with the dependents dwelling there or belonging to it, thirty-four [holdings], with all their appurtenances and adjacent properties.

Thus, from this day forward, the future rectors of that place shall hold and possess it for the adornment of the lights and the provision of ecclesiastical ornaments, for the remedy of the aforesaid boy’s soul, under the jurisdiction of that place; and they shall dispose of the other properties of the same church according to the needs of that place. For the sake of firmness concerning that same holy and venerable place, we have ordered these letters of ours to be drawn up as a solemn gift. Through them we decree and establish as valid and enduring that none of the faithful of the holy Church of God or of our own, present or future, presume to inflict any annoyance or opposition upon the aforesaid holy church on account of this estate written above or its appurtenances and adjacent properties.

Rather, may the rectors of that place enjoy it in peaceful possession for all time, governing it according to the needs of the same church, and may they earnestly pray for the forgiveness of the aforesaid boy and beseech the attainment of the glory of eternal blessedness, as well as our most felicitous safety granted by God. And so that this authority of ours may possess fuller force in the name of God, and be more diligently preserved and more truly believed by the faithful of the holy Church of God and by our own, we have confirmed it below with our own hand and ordered it to be authenticated below with the impression of our ring.

Sign of Lothar, most glorious Augustus.

I, Dructemirus, in place of Egilmarus, have reviewed and subscribed.

[Col. 1269D]

Given on the ninth day before the Kalends of February, in the twelfth year, with Christ’s favor, of the reign of the lord Lothar, emperor, in the thirteenth indiction. Done at the city of Pavia, prosperously in the name of God. Amen.

## CCVII. FOR THE CLERICS OF THE DIOCESE OF CREMONA (Year 835)

Emperor Lothar I, after an inquiry into the law, absolves the clerics of the diocese of Cremona, who complained that they had been compelled to provide packhorses and carts for the service of the imperial treasury, from this kind of burden.

[Muratori, *Antiquitates Italicae*, vol. II, p. 61.]

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, the eternal God, [Col. 1270A] Lothar, by the providence ordained by God, emperor Augustus.

If we willingly assent to the petitions of the servants of God when they make them known to our ears, and bring them to fulfillment, we confidently believe that this undoubtedly contributes to the increase of our reward and the attainment of eternal blessedness. Therefore, let it be known to all the faithful of the holy Church of God and of our own, present and future, that all the priests and the parish of Cremona, both from the rural churches and from the oratories, appearing before our presence, made known to our eminence that they had unjustly supplied packhorses and carts to be transported to our treasury.

We therefore ordered Ructaldus, our chaplain of the sacred palace, together with Maurinus, count of our palace, and also Count Adalgisus, to investigate carefully whether, according to justice, they ought to have provided those packhorses and carts for the performance of our service, or not. After investigating the matter most diligently, they reported to us that the priests had supplied the aforesaid packhorses and the same carts contrary to justice.

Therefore we command all our faithful that henceforth no one presume to bring any opposition against them concerning those packhorses or carts, either for the performance of our service or for that of any other person. Rather, let them be permitted to possess them and to pray more gladly for the mercy of the Lord on behalf of our safety and that of our wife and children. And so that this authority of ours may be held more firmly at all times and preserved inviolably in times to come, we ordered it to be sealed below with the impression of our ring.

There is no subscription by the emperor.

I, Dructemirus, subdeacon and notary, in place of Abumarius, have reviewed this.

Given on the Nones of March, in the seventeenth year, with Christ’s favor, of the reign of the lord Lothar, pious emperor, in the thirteenth indiction. Done at the royal palace of Sexpilas, prosperously in the name of God. Amen.

## CCVIII. FOR THE CHURCH OF ELNE (Year 836)

[In Baluze, *Appendix to Marca Hispanica*, col. 773.]

In the name of the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, Louis, by the clemency of God’s favor, [or: by God’s renewed favor], emperor Augustus.

If, for the love of God, we bestow suitable benefits upon places dedicated to divine worship and upon those serving Him in those places, we do not doubt that an eternal reward will be repaid to us by the Lord. Therefore, we wish it to be known to all our faithful, present and future, that the venerable Fulmo [Note: [Col. 1269D] He is called Ramno in the same charter, which Baluze had already published in a corrupted form; but it seems that this should be corrected to Salomon, who was already bishop in the year 832. For Count Beringarius, in the presence of Salomon the bishop, restored all the property of his monastery to Babilanus, abbot of Arles (Arulensis), by a deed of restoration made for him on the fourth day before the Nones of February, in the nineteenth year of the reign of our lord Louis the emperor. See *Marca Hispanica*, p. 769.] bishop of the church of Elne implored the mercy of our majesty that we should place the aforesaid see, with all that justly and legally belonged to it at the present time, under our protection and the defense of immunity, together with all its possessions: namely, the cell of Saint Felix, with all its boundaries and appurtenances; the estate called Torrente, another called Alamanis, and the spedulia [hostels/way-stations]; and, for the suitable needs of his church, the territory from Petrafita as far as its own enclosure; as well as the cell of Saint Julian; the lands which his men had brought out of the wilderness; and half of the pulveraticum (dust-tax) from the rafica [uncertain term], likewise from the market and from pasture dues. Let the careful understanding of all know that we have done this.
